title: Claims Recovery Accounting: Measuring What a Policyholder Is Asked to Send Back
content:
This is the accounting basis on which the money asked of a policyholder under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is measured. What she is asked to send back is what the supplement overpaid on the lines that fall outside cover, less what has been recovered from anyone else on them and less the balance those lines record standing to her credit, and it is never more than what reached her.

**What reached her.** Nothing is treated as having reached the policyholder.

**The overpayment.** The overpayment on those lines is then measured. Nothing is found overpaid.

**What has already come back from others.** What has already come back from others is then set against it. Nothing is set against it.

**The balance standing to her credit.** The balance those lines record standing to the policyholder's credit is set against it as well. She is credited with nothing.

**The figure.** What is asked of her is the overpayment less what has come back from others and less the balance credited to her, rounded to the cent once at the end, never more than what reached her and never less than nothing.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a policy whose claim record carries two paid crossover lines, the supplement having paid 96.00 on one and 84.00 on the other.

Nothing is treated as having reached the policyholder, so what reached her is 0.00. Nothing is found overpaid, so the overpayment is 0.00. Nothing is set against it for what has come back from others, and she is credited with nothing.

Taking nothing and nothing from an overpayment of 0.00 leaves 0.00, which is not less than nothing and is not more than the 0.00 that reached her. Rounded to the cent once at the end, what she is asked to send back is 0.00.
